rules.title: Every game piece has an owner.
rules.text: 1.7. Every game piece has an owner. Every game piece in play also has a controller.

rules.title: You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.).
rules.text: 1.7.1. You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.). You’re the “owner” of these pieces.

rules.title: You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area.
rules.text: 1.7.2. You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area. You’re the “controller” of these pieces, even if you’re not the owner.

rules.title: Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.
rules.text: 1.7.2.1. Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.

rules.title: Pieces your Rival controls are considered “rival” pieces.
rules.text: 1.7.2.2. Pieces your Rival controls are considered “rival” pieces.

rules.title: Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.
rules.text: 1.7.3. Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.

rules.title: When you take control of a Rival’s game piece, follow the rules in {GOLDEN RULES > Respect Your Rival}.
rules.text: 1.7.3.1. When you take control of a Rival’s game piece, follow the rules in Respect Your Rival.

rules.title: At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.
rules.text: 1.7.3.2. At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.

rules.title: If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
rules.text:
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.

> **EXAMPLE:** According to the rules, you can’t attack a ready Unit, but a friendly Unit’s card text reads “This Unit can attack ready Units.” The card text overrides that rule, so the friendly Unit can declare an attack on a rival ready Unit.

rules.title: If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect a…
rules.text:
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Rival plays a Unit with [ADRENALINE], which allows it to attack the turn it’s played. But a friendly Unit’s card text reads “Rival Units can't attack the turn they're played.” The preventing of the attack takes precedence, so the rival Unit can’t attack this turn.

rules.title: “Face-down” refers to a card displaying its back.
rules.text: 3.4. “Face-down” refers to a card displaying its back.

rules.title: While a card is face-down, ignore all card information, except whether or not the card is a Legend.
rules.text: 3.4.1. While a card is face-down, ignore all card information, except whether or not the card is a Legend. (As indicated by the cardback design.)

rules.title: To spend a ready card, turn it 90° until it is fully horizontal.
rules.text: 3.7. To spend a ready card, turn it 90° until it is fully horizontal.

rules.title: A card can be multiple types simultaneously.
rules.text: 4.2. A card can be multiple types simultaneously.

rules.title: Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.
rules.text: 4.2.1. Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.

rules.title: All 3 of your Legends begin face-down in your Legends area in a random order.
rules.text: 4.3. All 3 of your Legends begin face-down in your Legends area in a random order. See GAME SETUP > Pre-Game Setup.

rules.title: Once per turn, you may Call a Legend to flip a Legend face-up.
rules.text: 4.3.1. Once per turn, you may Call a Legend to flip a Legend face-up. See TERMS > Game Actions > Call a Legend.

rules.title: A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area.
rules.text: 4.4. A Legend is only valid in the Legends area or field area. All other areas (trash, hand, deck, etc.) are invalid areas.

rules.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.
rules.text: 4.4.1. If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game.

rules.title: If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending.
rules.text: 4.4.2. If a Legend moves to an invalid area, any effects that trigger from the card entering the area enter pending. Remove the Legend from the game before you resolve them. See GAME AREAS > Removed from Game.

rules.title: You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.
rules.text: 4.5. You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.

rules.title: A Legend played in this way enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area.
rules.text: 4.5.1. A Legend played in this way enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area.

rules.title: A Legend played in this way enters with Lag.
rules.text: 4.5.2. A Legend played in this way enters with Lag. See Lag.

rules.title: Legends with cost Null ( - ) do not have a cost, and cannot be played to the field.
rules.text: 4.5.3. Legends with cost Null ( - ) do not have a cost, and cannot be played to the field. See Cost Value.

rules.title: To play a Unit, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and place it ready in the field area.
rules.text: 4.6. To play a Unit, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and place it ready in the field area.

rules.title: Units enter the field with Lag.
rules.text: 4.7. Units enter the field with Lag. See Lag.

rules.title: To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
rules.text: 4.10. To play a Gear, reveal the card to your Rival, pay its cost, and equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend. See Equip.

rules.title: By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.
rules.text: 4.10.1. By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

rules.title: You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.
rules.text: 4.10.2. You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.

rules.title: There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.
rules.text: 4.10.3. There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.

rules.title: Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”
rules.text: 4.11. Gears have two textboxes, referred to as the “top textbox” and “bottom textbox.”

rules.title: The top textbox contains effects for the Gear.
rules.text: 4.11.1. The top textbox contains effects for the Gear. These effects are relevant when you play the Gear, and generally not relevant after a Gear is equipped.

rules.title: Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equip…
rules.text:
4.11.2. Effects described in the top textbox apply to the Gear itself, and are not inherited by the Unit or Legend it’s equipped to.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Gear’s top text box contains the reminder text “*(Equip to a friendly Unit or face-up Legend.)*” You equip this Gear to a friendly Unit. That Gear cannot be equipped to another friendly Unit, nor face-up Legend.

rules.title: The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to.
rules.text: 4.11.3. The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to. Read the bottom textbox as if it's printed on that Unit or Legend.

rules.title: Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the G…
rules.text: 4.11.3.1. Effects described in a Gear card’s bottom textbox apply only to the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to, not the Gear itself.

rules.title: A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.
rules.text: 4.11.3.2. A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.

rules.title: When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.
rules.text: 4.12. When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

rules.title: When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to t…
rules.text:
4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

rules.title: If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new a…
rules.text: 4.12.2. If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new area. The Gear is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend from play.

rules.title: When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order.
rules.text: 4.12.3. When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order. Randomize them amongst any other cards bottom-decked at the same time. See Bottom-deck.

rules.title: A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”
rules.text: 5.3. A game area may be “public” or “hidden.”

rules.title: If a game area is public, these rules apply.
rules.text: 5.3.1. If a game area is public, these rules apply.

rules.title: Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players.
rules.text: 5.3.1.1. Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players. You can look at information on all face-up cards at any time.

rules.title: Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known.
rules.text: 5.3.1.2. Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

rules.title: If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.
rules.text: 5.3.2. If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.

rules.title: Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known.
rules.text: 5.3.2.1. Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

rules.title: If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.
rules.text: 5.3.2.2. If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to…
rules.text: 5.3.2.3. If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to another area.

rules.title: When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fai…
rules.text: 5.3.2.4. When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fail to find a valid target. See Search.

rules.title: If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may cho…
rules.text: 5.3.2.4.1. If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may choose to fail to find a target.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choo…
rules.text: 5.3.2.5. If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choose a legal target. You are not required to reveal it.

rules.title: If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not cho…
rules.text: 5.3.2.6. If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not chosen, return those cards to their original area in their original order and state.

rules.title: Field Area
rules.text: 5.6. ### Field Area

rules.title: The field area may be referred to as just “field” or “your field” (and variations thereof).
rules.text: 5.6.1. The field area may be referred to as just “field” or “your field” (and variations thereof).

rules.title: Play a card by paying its cost and placing it ready on the field.
rules.text: 5.6.2. Play a card by paying its cost and placing it ready on the field.

rules.title: All cards played are to the field area unless specified otherwise.
rules.text: 5.6.2.1. All cards played are to the field area unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: A card in the field is “in play.”
rules.text: 5.6.2.2. A card in the field is “in play.”

rules.title: The field is a public area.
rules.text: 5.6.3. The field is a public area. You can look at the face-up cards any player has on their field at any time. You may always know the number of cards any player has in play.

rules.title: Units and Legends enter the field with a condition called “Lag.” See Lag.
rules.text: 5.6.4. Units and Legends enter the field with a condition called “Lag.” See Lag.

rules.title: There is no limit on the amount of Units you can have in the Field area.
rules.text: 5.6.5. There is no limit on the amount of Units you can have in the Field area.

rules.title: Legends Area
rules.text: 5.7. ### Legends Area

rules.title: Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.
rules.text: 5.7.1. Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.

rules.title: You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.
rules.text: 5.7.2. You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.

rules.title: While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.
rules.text: 5.7.2.1. While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.

rules.title: If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.
rules.text: 5.7.2.2. If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.

rules.title: “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.
rules.text: 5.7.3. “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.

rules.title: The Legends area is a public area.
rules.text: 5.7.4. The Legends area is a public area. Players can count the number of cards any player has in this area and read them at any time.

rules.title: The face-down Legends in this area are hidden.
rules.text: 5.7.4.1. The face-down Legends in this area are hidden. You cannot look at them unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival…
rules.text: 5.7.4.2. If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival without revealing them. This can be with a token marker, or by physically separating known Legends from unknown Legends.

rules.title: If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unles…
rules.text: 5.7.4.3. If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unless otherwise specified.

rules.title: You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit.
rules.text: 5.7.5. You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit. See CARD TYPES > Legends.

rules.title: A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.
rules.text: 5.7.6. A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.

rules.title: There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.
rules.text: 5.7.7. There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.

rules.title: Trash Area
rules.text: 5.9. ### Trash Area

rules.title: The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).
rules.text: 5.9.1. The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).

rules.title: The trash is a public area.
rules.text: 5.9.2. The trash is a public area.

rules.title: Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these ca…
rules.text: 5.9.3. Cards in this area are placed face-up in a pile, and either player can freely view the contents and order of these cards.

rules.title: When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.
rules.text: 5.9.4. When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.

rules.title: If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.
rules.text: 5.9.4.1. If multiple cards enter this area at the same time, their owner adds them in any order.

rules.title: Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash.
rules.text: 5.9.4.2. Players may freely change the order of cards in their own trash. The cards in the trash should always remain in the face-up position unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: During your Main phase, you may take valid Main phase actions in any order.
rules.text: 8.10. During your Main phase, you may take valid Main phase actions in any order.

rules.title: Unless stated otherwise, you may take any action any number of times.
rules.text: 8.10.1. Unless stated otherwise, you may take any action any number of times.

rules.title: Play a Card
rules.text:
8.13. ### Play a Card

As an action during your Main phase, you may play a card from your hand. See Play.

rules.title: Activate an Effect
rules.text:
8.14. ### Activate an Effect

As an action during your Main phase, you may activate any activated effects on friendly Units or Legends. They may be used during the open state of the main phase. For the full rules on activating effects, see EFFECTS > Activated Effects.

rules.title: You cannot activate [Spend Icon] effects on Lagging Units.
rules.text: 8.14.1. You cannot activate [Spend Icon] effects on Lagging Units. See Lag.

rules.title: Attack
rules.text:
8.15. ### Attack

As an action during your Main phase, you may attack with a Unit. For the full rules on attacking, see ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL.

rules.title: When your turn ends, you must resolve any end of turn effects in this order.
rules.text: 8.16. When your turn ends, you must resolve any end of turn effects in this order.

rules.title: Resolve effects that occur “at the end of your turn,” “at the end of each turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.text: 8.16.1. Resolve effects that occur “at the end of your turn,” “at the end of each turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.title: Remove effects that last “this turn” and variations thereof.
rules.text: 8.16.2. Remove effects that last “this turn” and variations thereof.

rules.title: When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, if Overtime conditions are met, Overtime immediately…
rules.text: 8.17. When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, if Overtime conditions are met, Overtime immediately begins.

rules.title: When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, your Rival’s turn begins automatically.
rules.text: 8.18. When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, your Rival’s turn begins automatically.

rules.title: ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL
rules.text: ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL

rules.title: “Attack” is a game action in which you spend a friendly ready Unit to attack a valid target, which results in the fri…
rules.text: 9.1. “Attack” is a game action in which you spend a friendly ready Unit to attack a valid target, which results in the friendly Unit fighting or stealing.

rules.title: You may attack as a Main Phase action.
rules.text: 9.2. You may attack as a Main Phase action. See TURN ORDER > Main Phase.

rules.title: To attack, you must declare the attack by completing these steps in order.
rules.text: 9.3. To attack, you must declare the attack by completing these steps in order.

rules.title: Choose a friendly ready Unit in the field area that can attack.
rules.text: 9.3.1. Choose a friendly ready Unit in the field area that can attack.

rules.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
rules.text: 9.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack. See Lag.

rules.title: Choose a valid attack target for that Unit.
rules.text: 9.3.2. Choose a valid attack target for that Unit.

rules.title: A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target.
rules.text: 9.3.2.1. A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target.

rules.title: A rival Gig area containing one or more Gigs is a valid attack target.
rules.text: 9.3.2.2. A rival Gig area containing one or more Gigs is a valid attack target. (An empty Gig area is not a valid attack target.)

rules.title: Card effects may add to, remove, or restrict a Unit’s valid attack targets.
rules.text: 9.3.2.3. Card effects may add to, remove, or restrict a Unit’s valid attack targets.

rules.title: An effect that allows a Unit to attack only grants the specific permission described by that effect and does not remo…
rules.text: 9.3.2.3.1. An effect that allows a Unit to attack only grants the specific permission described by that effect and does not remove other attack restrictions.

rules.title: If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack.
rules.text: 9.3.2.4. If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack.

rules.title: Spend the friendly Unit.
rules.text: 9.3.3. Spend the friendly Unit.

rules.title: Communicate the attack and the attack target to your Rival.
rules.text: 9.3.4. Communicate the attack and the attack target to your Rival.

rules.title: When you declare an attack to your Rival, the game process of “attacking” begins immediately.
rules.text: 9.4. When you declare an attack to your Rival, the game process of “attacking” begins immediately.

rules.title: While attacking, you are the “attacking player.”
rules.text: 9.4.1. While attacking, you are the “attacking player.”

rules.title: While you’re attacking, your Rival is the “defending player.”
rules.text: 9.4.2. While you’re attacking, your Rival is the “defending player.”

rules.title: The Unit you spend to attack is the “attacker” or “attacking Unit.” It attacks the selected target.
rules.text: 9.4.3. The Unit you spend to attack is the “attacker” or “attacking Unit.” It attacks the selected target.

rules.title: If your attack target is a Unit, it’s called the “defending Unit,” “defender,” or “opposing Unit.”
rules.text: 9.4.4. If your attack target is a Unit, it’s called the “defending Unit,” “defender,” or “opposing Unit.”

rules.title: If your attack target is the rival Gig area, it’s called the “defending Gig area.”
rules.text: 9.4.5. If your attack target is the rival Gig area, it’s called the “defending Gig area.”

rules.title: When you declare the attack to your Rival, apply effects that last “while attacking” and variations thereof.
rules.text: 9.5. When you declare the attack to your Rival, apply effects that last “while attacking” and variations thereof. All effects triggered by attacking or spending the attacker become pending. See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution}.

rules.title: After all pending effects are resolved, if the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the att…
rules.text: 9.6. After all pending effects are resolved, if the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack. Otherwise, the attack continues; proceed to the React Step.

rules.title: During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react.
rules.text: 9.7. During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react. They may take as many reactions as they want, in any order they choose.

rules.title: You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.
rules.text: 9.7.1. You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.

rules.title: You may Call a Legend as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.8. You may Call a Legend as a reaction. See Call a Legend.

rules.title: You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.9. You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.

rules.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.
rules.text: 9.9.1. When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.

rules.title: You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.10. You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction. See TERMS > Effect Keywords > QUICK.

rules.title: If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.
rules.text: 9.10.1. If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.

rules.title: If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending.
rules.text: 9.11. If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before the defending player may take another reaction. See EFFECTS > Triggered Effects.

rules.title: At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, th…
rules.text: 9.12. At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, the defending player may choose to end the React Step.

rules.title: If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends.
rules.text: 9.13. If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack.

rules.title: When the React Step ends, the attack continues.
rules.text: 9.14. When the React Step ends, the attack continues. If the attack target is a Unit, proceed to the Fight Step. If the attack target is a Gig area, proceed to the Steal Step.

rules.title: The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit.
rules.text: 9.15. The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit. If the attack target is a Gig Area, the Steal Step happens instead.

rules.title: During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.
rules.text: 9.16. During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.

rules.title: At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.
rules.text: 9.16.1. At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.

rules.title: A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially…
rules.text: 9.17. A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially one winner.

rules.title: A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.
rules.text: 9.17.1. A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.

rules.title: When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.
rules.text: 9.17.1.1. When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.

rules.title: A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.
rules.text: 9.17.2. A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.

rules.title: If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.
rules.text: 9.17.3. If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.

rules.title: If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power com…
rules.text: 9.17.4. If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power comparison.

rules.title: When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e.

rules.title: The [Spend Icon] symbol is shorthand for an activation cost.
rules.text:
11.15.1. The [Spend Icon] symbol is shorthand for an activation cost. It means: “Spend this Unit or Legend to activate the following effect.”

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit has the effect “[Spend Icon] Draw 1.” The [Spend Icon] symbol is an activation trigger. You must specifically spend this Unit as a cost. If you do, you draw a card.

faqFindings.finding: Go Solo is permitted in the CALL turn.
The entering Legend may fund its own Go Solo.
Ordinary play remains available alongside Go Solo.
Field-entry turn does not permit Spend-icon effects.
Ordinary entry pays numeric cost, preserves orientation, and applies Lag.
V may enter through ordinary play.
Legend field play qualifies for Jackie.
Go Solo cannot override an opposing attack prohibition.
Gear follows the host departure and stays when the Legend is subsequently removed.
Dying Night benefit survives defeat of its attacking V host.
Zero Gig decrease still creates the later benefit.
A newly played Unit may Block.
Hands Unclean cannot use its printed Blocker in the Legends area.
